map.Lessons 7-4, 7-5 & 7-6 — part of the Bel: Lessons 7-4, 7-5 & 7-6 are part of the Below Zero arc. four quadrants · distance · polygons · 6.NOS.C.6/8 · 6.GR.A.3. Read from start to end. Each gate gives hints and a worked example. It never blocks the page.
map.Episode 3. Same crew, same city — one fo: Episode 3. Same crew, same city. One part of the case. Turn the page when you're ready.
map.Ada's map cuts the city into four quadra: Ada's map has four quadrants. Count counterclockwise from the upper right: I, II, III, IV.
map.Every station is an ordered pair (x, y):: Every station is an ordered pair (x, y). Go east–west first, then north–south. (2, 5) is NOT (5, 2).
map.Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and: Two relays must light next: (−3, 2) and (4, −1). The blackout mixed up my map. Five dots flicker, but only two are real.
map.An ordered pair (x, y) locates a point:: An ordered pair (x, y) names a point. x is first (left–right), then y (up–down).
map.Read the pairs carefully, reader. Light: Read the pairs with care, reader. If we light the wrong relay, we waste power.
map.Five dots flicker on Ada's map, but only: Five dots flicker on Ada's map. Only the relays at (−3, 2) and (4, −1) are real. Tap to light exactly those two. Tap again to turn one off. Then name their quadrants.
map.Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). T: Conceptual: an ordered pair is (x, y). From the origin, the first number moves left (negative) or right (positive). The second moves down (negative) or up (positive).
map.Procedural: walk each pair: for (−1, 4): Procedural: walk each pair. For (−1, 4), go 1 block left, then 4 blocks up. Quadrants count counterclockwise from the upper right: I, then II, then III, then IV.
map.Cable time. Even elevation runs below ze: Cable time. Even the height goes below zero down here. The old platform is at −6 meters.
map.When two points share a coordinate, the: Two points can share a coordinate. Then the path between them is straight. Measure it with absolute values.
map.Conceptual: when two points share a coor: Conceptual: two points share a coordinate, so the cable runs straight. If the numbers that change are on OPPOSITE sides of zero, ADD their absolute values. On the same side of zero? SUBTRACT them.
map.Procedural: like (−4, 1) to (2, 1): x cr: Procedural: take (−4, 1) to (2, 1). x crosses zero, so |−4| + |2| = 6 blocks. Take (7, −2) to (7, −9). It stays on one side, so 9 − 2 = 7 blocks.
map.Midnight. One move left: ring the engine: Midnight. One move left: circle the engine district with cable, and the whole grid lights up.
map.Width, height, then total cable. Three l: Width, height, then total cable. Three locks, one ring. Reader, get us home.
map.Boss Gate: distances on the plane, plus: Boss Gate: find distances on the plane. Then find the perimeter of a polygon on the grid.
map.The ring's corner relays: (−4, −2), (3,: The ring's corner relays: (−4, −2), (3, −2), (3, 3), (−4, 3). Open all three locks to finish the circuit:
map.Conceptual: a side's length is the dista: Conceptual: a side's length is the distance between the coordinates that CHANGE. If they are on opposite sides of zero, add the two distances. The perimeter is the whole trip around all four sides.
map.Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6: Procedural: a side from x = −2 to x = 6 crosses zero, so 2 + 6 = 8 blocks. Perimeter shortcut: 2 × (width + height).
Twenty-four blocks of cable, none to spare. We counted and checked.
map.Achievement unlocked: city un-frozen. Ho: Achievement unlocked: the city is warm! The cocoa race starts now.
map.New distortion below city hall. A door s: A new distortion is below city hall. A door shaped like a balance scale. It wants things EQUAL. To be continued…
map.completed Unit 7 · Episode 3: The Grid M: completed Unit 7 · Episode 3: The Grid Map in the Below Zero arc, and showed they know four quadrants · distance · polygons · 6.NOS.C.6/8 · 6.GR.A.3.
map.Left and down lands in Quadrant III — th: Left and down is Quadrant III. There, both signs are negative.
map.Your turn — same idea, different numbers: Your turn. Same idea, new numbers:
map.x goes from −6 to 3 — opposite sides of: x goes from −6 to 3. These are opposite sides of zero, so add the distances: |−6| + |3| = 9 blocks.
map.Now (4, −1) to (4, −7): both y-values ar: Now (4, −1) to (4, −7). Both y-values are below zero, on the same side, so subtract: 7 − 1 = 6 blocks.
map.Width: x runs from −1 to 3, crossing zer: Width: x goes from −1 to 3 and crosses zero, so 1 + 3 = 4. Height: y goes from −2 to 1, so 2 + 1 = 3.
map.A grid rectangle is 6 wide and 3 tall. H: A grid rectangle is 6 wide and 3 tall. How much cable goes around it?
map.The second number is the up–down move: (: The second number is the up–down move. (−3, 2) goes UP 2. It does not go down.
map.Re-walk each pair from the origin: left–: Walk each pair again from the origin: left–right first, then up–down.
map.Relays lit! Now the quadrants — count co: Relays lit! Now the quadrants. Count counterclockwise from the upper right: I, II, III, IV.
map.(−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II and (4, −1): (−3, 2) glows in Quadrant II and (4, −1) in Quadrant IV. The relays link up across the city!
map.Cable A crosses x = 0 — don't subtract s: Cable A crosses x = 0. Do not subtract across zero. Add each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Both y-values sit on the SAME side of ze: Both y-values are on the SAME side of zero. Subtract the smaller distance from the bigger one.
map.Cable B runs up–down: only the y-numbers: Cable B goes up–down. Only the y-numbers change. Count with care below zero.
map.8 blocks across, 5 blocks down — both ca: 8 blocks across, 5 blocks down. Both cables are measured, with no extra!
map.Lock 1 holds. Width: x runs from −4 to 3: Lock 1 is still shut. Width: x goes from −4 to 3, opposite sides of zero. ADD each end's distance from the y-axis.
map.Lock 2 holds. Height: y runs from −2 up: Lock 2 is still shut. Height: y goes from −2 up to 3, opposite sides again. Add the distances.
map.Lock 3 holds. 35 is the AREA inside the: Lock 3 is still shut. 35 is the AREA inside the ring. The cable goes around the EDGE. Add all four sides.
map.Lock 3 holds. That's one width plus one: Lock 3 is still shut. That is one width plus one height. The ring needs BOTH widths and BOTH heights.
map.Lock 3 holds. Perimeter is the whole tri: Lock 3 is still shut. Perimeter is the whole trip around: width + height + width + height.
map.ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable close: ALL LOCKS OPEN. 24 blocks of cable finish the ring. The Light Ring blazes and Axiom City lights up, quadrant by quadrant!
